title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Aldrich is an expansive sludge of maggot-ridden rotten flesh, humanity dregs, and his own bones as well as those of the victims he has consumed.

By the time the player reaches him, he will be inert and spread across the floor, using the weapons and malformed body of Gwyndolin to interact with his environment and perform attacks.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldrich was once a cleric of the Way of White originating from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, implying that he may have been a descendant of the gods of Anor Londo. Despite his status as a man of faith serving the gods, he was actually a depraved cleric who took pleasure in devouring humans and indulging in their last screams. For the cleric, eating people became a routine, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: of the resurrected Lords of Cinder, Aldrich had no intention of sacrificing himself anew, as he had come to believe that an "Age of the Deep" should come and replace the Age of Fire, motivating him to try to devour the gods themselves to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep, Aldrich, still hungry for flesh and now eager to devour Gods, marched on Irithyll with his followers so that he could devour Gwyndolin, the king of the Gods. He found his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White without a fight. Aldrich emerged victorious from the ensuing battle, slaughtering Sulyvahn\'s troops and forcing the Pontiff to reluctantly clear the way for the ruined cathedral of Anor Londo. Having finally reached his prey, Aldrich began to slowly devour Gwyndolin, who was most likely powerless to fight

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Aldrich's throne in Firelink Shrine refers to him as "Saint Aldrich of the Deep".
Before eating Gwyndolin, Aldrich imposed on himself a practice of asceticism (苦行), that is, he refrained from eating humans before he could devour the god.
During the fight, as well as when the boss is passive, shrieks and moans of pain can be heard coming from Gwyndolin. As Aldrich was half-way through consuming Gwyndolin and had used the God's body to defend himself, this disturbingly implies that Gwyndolin was still alive (albeit barely) and in a semi-conscious state of being continuously devoured by Aldrich, even during the fight.
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The encounter begins with Aldrich standing on the far end of the room, imbuing his staff with magic and wielding it menacingly while he prepares for battle. He specializes in ranged combat, doing so by casting diverse dangerous magical spells. Conversely, his close combat abilities become heavily compromised due to his sluggish mobility and tendency to miss hits with his weapon. His substandard melee abilities should not be underestimated, however, because what he lacks in accuracy, he more than makes it up in damage-dealing potential.

When he rears up and aims his bow, he will launch an expanding wave of highly damaging arrows in front of him, allowing you to circle behind him and get hits in.

title: The Deep
snippet: aldrich_devourer_of_gods_aldrich_saint_of_the_deep : The "peaceful and sacred" Deep would be sharply transformed with the arrival of Aldrich, a Way of White cleric who was practically exiled from his home. Originating from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, Aldrich was ostensibly a proper man of cloth; however, despite his appearance and status, he was in fact a depraved cleric who took pleasure in devouring humans and indulging in their last screams. Eating people became a routine for Aldrich, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge. With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : At the beginning of the fight, charge at Aldrich to avoid his hard-hitting soul spear. Get behind him and focus your attacks on his tail. This leaves him with nothing to do but swing his two slow, devastating melee attacks or teleport across the room (usually, adjacent to where he teleported from).

At about 55%-60% health, he will teleport and come back up, buffed with fire. His arrows also go from going forward to following a specific player. If the arrows following the player catch up to them, then that player will most likely go down quick. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended for this fight.

Casting the sorcery Twisted Wall of Light can negate Aldrich's ranged attacks, including his arrow barrage in the second phase, allowing one to wait out the attack by casting repeatedly.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.
The comic *Dark Souls: The Breath of Andolus* features a scryer named Aldrich as the deuteragonist, potentially as a reference to him, despite them not being the same character. Alternatively, it may have been Aldrich long in the past, given he begins to adopt Aldrich's characteristics, such as cannibalism. While he claims to have been forced into it, the scryer Aldrich is later revealed to be a two faced schemer.
The music played during his fight is a more sinister and macabre arrangement of Gwyndolin's theme from the first game, as he uses the body of the god to defend himself, there are also elements from Nito's theme that are played in the first phase as displayed by the sinister chants and piano notes that are also prevalent in Nito's theme.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the many children that Aldrich had when he was trapped inside the Cathedral of the Deep were the results of repeated violence on Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth. Rosaria's room is covered with cradles and Aldrich was already known for having had multiple children, of whom Anri and Horace are the only survivors. Additionally, Rosaria's soul has a broken and twisted appearance, and Ringfinger Leonhard talks about how his goddess's body has been violated.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

snippet: When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: In *Scholar of the First Sin*, Aldia, the older brother of King Vendrick, hints at a path for the Bearer of the Curse that differs from the one presented to them. If the conditions are met, he can serve as the final boss of *Dark Souls II*, with his fight triggering after Nashandra's; he, notably, is the only boss in any *Dark Souls* game not to die when defeated, and as such drops no souls nor items, with the player instead gaining the option of an alternate ending in which the Bearer of the Curse is hinted to as following this mysterious other path at Aldia's side. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via the Soul Stream description, which refers to him as "**the first of the Scholars**". He is voiced by David Gant, who also voiced Oswald of Carim in *Dark Souls*.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Gods** or **Deities** are a storyline concept in the *Dark Souls *series. They are beings, real or fictional, who have been worshipped as Gods throughout the Ages.

A number of them, the **Gods of Anor Londo** or "**Old Gods**", are (or once were) real, and members of the unnamed species of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, including his direct relatives. The Gods of Anor Londo took on the roles of Deities served by the smaller Humans, mainly through the Way of White, the most widespread Human religion, with Gwyn as its central omnipotent figure.

 dark_souls_iii : Even after the awakening of the Ashen One, the influence of several gods or their descendants is still present in the world.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin, once the king of the gods and of Irithyll, had been imprisoned in the city's old cathedral by Pontiff Sulyvahn, that stripped him of his power to rule in his place. However Aldrich, Devourer of Gods had arrived in Irithyll and, after defeating Sulyvahn, he began to devour Gwyndolin. Yorshka, Gwyndolin'sister, is still alive and leads the knights's of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant, but she has been imprisoned by Sulyvahn in an isolated tower.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Perhaps the most telling of their fall were the number of foot soldiers tasked with the covert disposal of corrupted members. As the Abyss slowly morphed the Legion's lost members, the so-called "Followers" would be sent to execute them before they were transformed into abyssal beasts. Their primary technique was to surround the target, burning and stabbing them, and finishing them with honor using javelins thrown with great force.

Beneath their home in Farron Keep are the Catacombs of Carthus, which contain a chalice holding High Lord Wolnir, who fell to the Abyss long ago. Along with the cindered Smouldering Lake, nearby is the Cathedral of the Deep, resting place of Aldrich, Devourer of Gods.

title: Ashen One
snippet: firelink_shrine_dark_souls_iii_firelink_shrine : Inside the shrine, they encounter the Fire Keeper, who tells the Ashen One that the Lords of Cinder—Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Lothric, Younger Prince—have abandoned their thrones, and charges them with bringing the lords back. The Fire Keeper offers to channel souls in order to increase the Ashen One's strength. Also in the shrine are Blacksmith Andre, a smith from the Age of Gods; the Shrine Handmaid, who offers an expanding store of goods in exchange for souls; Hawkwood the Deserter, a crestfallen warrior; Ludleth of Courland, the last remaining Lord of Cinder who offers the Ashen One advice and the art of soul transposition (provided the Ashen One can provide him with a Transposing Kiln); and Nestling, a bird who offers to trade items. title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After the death of the Blacksmith Deity who was responsible for forging the weapons and armor of the gods, his task was assigned to a giant who thus became the new blacksmith of the gods, and came to work and reside inside the cathedral of Anor Londo. Among many things, he was responsible for creating the Dragonslayer Greatarrows and the Dragonslayer Lightning Arrows used by dragonslayers during the sporting hunts of the age of the gods. He also created Lightning Bolts infused with the power of lightning made for humans' crossbows, as during those times humans were still servants of the gods.

title: Soul of Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Soul of Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - item - trivia 
 trivia : A more accurate translation of "主神" would be "king god/main deity". This confirms the fact that Gwyndolin, the god who is devoured by Aldrich, had effectively become the leader of the gods of ancient Anor Londo and obtained the place at the helm of the Way of White. To do this he would have to overthrow Allfather Lloyd, Gwyn's uncle who had assumed command while Gwyndolin was still considered a "daughter" of Gwyn.

title: Wolf Knight's Greatsword
snippet:
As implied by its description, the Wolf Knight's Greatsword deals increased damage against foes that originate from the Abyss, such as Darkwraiths. This also encompasses six bosses:
Iudex Gundyr*
High Lord Wolnir
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
Dragonslayer Armour
Darkeater Midir
Phase 1 of Slave Knight Gael
